videos.script: A planner asks a server for a course, and the answer takes a while. The program must not stand still while it waits. {{why}} First, the old way. A function takes a closure and calls it later. It works, and the code drifts to the right with every step. {{await}} Then the new way. Async marks a function that can pause. Await marks where it pauses. The same program reads top to bottom again. {{task}} Then the task, which starts asynchronous work from ordinary code. And a task nobody waited for, which simply never finished. {{parallel}} Then two ways to do several things at once. Async let, for a fixed handful. A task group, for a whole list. The clock shows nine hundred milliseconds become three hundred. {{cancel}} Last, cancellation. It is a request, not an order. You will watch one loop ignore it and finish anyway, and another stop where it should. By the end, the planner loads a week of courses at once, and stops when nobody wants the answer.
